newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to investigate mobile phone health danger.
newsitem.headline: Australia to investigate mobile phone health danger.

text.p: The Australian government on Tuesday announced a A$4.5 million (US$3.5 million) programme to investigate potential dangers to health from using mobile telephones and related equipment.

Communications Minister Richard Alston said the five-year study, funded by an increase in radio communications licence fees, followed community concern about the effect of mobile phones, mobile phone towers and other equipment.

"Sections of the public are concerned about possible adverse health effects from long-term exposure to radiofrequency electromagnetic energy -- especially in regard to children -- with the increased use of radio-based communications technologies, such as mobile phones," Alston said in a statement.
Health Minister David Wooldridge said in a statement there was no substantial evidence available of health dangers from mobile phones, but said more research was needed.
The study programme will be contracted out to private and government groups in a range of areas, including scientific bodies, universities and hospitals.
